overall: The AG found the Holland Board of Health did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no executive session was ever convened, deliberation evidence was insufficient, and the late minutes claim was declined. Reminders issued, no orders.

allegations.summary: Two Board members allegedly discussed bringing charges against a Board member outside an open meeting, citing a remark made during the April 23 joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Even if we were to accept that this statement was made, however, such a comment is not sufficient to establish that Ms. Manning and Mr. Ference engaged in improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Two Board members allegedly improperly entered executive session at the April 23 joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes show that no vote to enter executive session took place.

allegations.summary: A Board member allegedly was improperly excluded from an executive session that was sought at the April 23 joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As stated both above and in the minutes, no executive session took place.

allegations.summary: Two Board members allegedly sought to discuss Open Meeting Law complaints against a Board member in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: In the request for further review, the complainant alleged the April 23 minutes contained inaccuracies, a claim not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation, as it was not raised in the initial complaint filed with the Board.
